transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… mostly I’m here because I keep getting pulled off track really easily. Like, I’ll be trying to finish a dashboard, and then a Slack ping or even just a song lyric or some random project idea comes up, and I lose the thread. It’s been… frustrating.
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily in other situations too, like during meetings or while reading, or does this mainly happen when you're working on tasks like dashboards?

Mostly with the dashboard-type stuff, I guess. It’s like… one Slack ping, or even a song lyric getting stuck in my head, or some random idea for another project, and then I’ve kind of lost where I was. I haven’t really thought about it much beyond that.
Have you noticed yourself getting distracted easily in other parts of your life, like during conversations or while watching something, or does this mainly stay limited to when you're working?

I think it’s mainly when I’m working, yeah. Like with the dashboard stuff… a Slack ping, or even a song lyric or some random project idea, and then I lose where I was. I haven’t really tracked it much outside of that.
Have you noticed a lack of interest or pleasure in activities that you usually enjoy?
Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things I usually like.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless at any point recently, even outside of work?
Not really… I mean, I get stressed or frustrated sometimes, but I haven’t noticed feeling hopeless or really sad outside of that.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble staying seated during the day?
Yeah… somewhat. If I’m stuck on a long Zoom call or trying to work quietly in one spot, I start feeling this kind of pressure to get up or pace, or I need to do something with my hands.
Looking back, did you have similar issues with staying focused or getting distracted when you were in school or doing homework as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t remember all of it, but even in elementary school teachers would write stuff like I rushed through worksheets or didn’t follow all the directions. My parents also had to sit with me for homework a lot, because I’d kind of drift off or start doing something else before I finished.
Do you ever find it hard to pick up on social cues, like when someone is not interested in what you're saying, or have trouble understanding how your behavior affects others?

Sometimes, yeah. Like in group projects, when people are brainstorming, I’ll jump in with my idea before they’re done explaining. Or I might start adding things to the Figma board too soon. I usually realize after that it probably came off kind of pushy, even though I was just excited.

Outside of work tasks like the dashboards, do you ever find yourself struggling to stay focused or feeling overly restless during other daily activities, like chores, hobbies, or even while having conversations?

Yeah… I guess with reading or videos, too. Like I’ll sit down to read a research article, or watch a UX tutorial, and after a few minutes I realize I’ve been looking at the words or the screen but I didn’t actually take anything in.
Can you think of any examples where you've had trouble staying focused or felt very restless outside of work or structured tasks—like when you're at home, with friends, or doing something you enjoy?

Yeah… at home, mostly. Like if I try to just read for fun or do a quiet sketching thing, I don’t really stay with it calmly. I’ll start talking to myself, or put music on, or check something on my phone. Sometimes it turns into a whole bigger project instead of just… relaxing with it.

Would you say these issues with staying focused and feeling restless happen in most areas of your life, like at work, at home, and when you’re with other people, or are they mostly limited to certain situations?

It’s… not just one situation, I don’t think. It shows up enough that it’s affected things. I’ve lost a couple small freelance contracts, and I missed out on a portfolio competition because I didn’t really follow through cleanly.

And with friends or people I collaborate with, some of them are a little hesitant to work with me now. They still like my ideas, I think, but they don’t always trust me to be reliable with the actual follow-through.

Would you say these issues with staying focused and feeling restless have been happening consistently for most of your life, or do you feel like they’ve gotten noticeably worse in recent years, especially outside of work stressors?

I think it’s been there for a long time. Like, not just recently.

Even in elementary school, teachers would write comments about me rushing through worksheets or not keeping track of directions. And I guess I talked over other kids during group work sometimes. My parents also had to sit next to me for homework, because I’d kind of wander off or start doing something else before finishing.
Can you describe a time when you had trouble staying focused or felt restless in a setting that wasn’t work-related, like at home, in a social situation, or during a hobby?

Yeah… I guess when I’m at home and I try to read, or just do a simple sketching exercise to calm down, I don’t really stay with it quietly.

I’ll start talking to myself, or put music on, or check my phone for something. Sometimes the sketch turns into this bigger project, and then it’s not really relaxing anymore.
Can you think of a time when you experienced trouble staying focused or felt restless in a setting that wasn’t at home or at work, like in a social situation or during a public event?

Yeah… during hackathon check-ins, or when I’m waiting in office-hour lines, I get pretty antsy. I’ll keep checking the time, shifting around, and sometimes I have to stop myself from jumping in before it’s actually my turn.
Have you ever had trouble staying focused or felt overly restless during activities outside of work or home, like in public places, social gatherings, or while running errands?

Yeah… mostly in lines or waiting situations. Like at hackathon check-ins or office hours, I get really antsy. I keep checking the time, shifting around, and I have to stop myself from jumping in before it’s actually my turn.

Can you describe how your difficulty staying focused and feeling restless impacts your daily life outside of specific work or waiting situations—like when you're interacting with friends, managing personal responsibilities, or trying to relax?

It’s… mostly that people don’t always trust me to follow through, I guess.

I’ve lost a couple small freelance-type things because I didn’t finish cleanly or keep things organized enough. And I missed out on a portfolio competition for similar reasons. Friends or people I collaborate with still like my ideas, but they’re more hesitant to actually work with me now.
Can you recall any specific times when you had trouble staying focused or felt restless while in a social gathering or public place, like a café, party, or event?

Yeah… I guess the main thing is when I’m waiting my turn, like at hackathon check-ins or in office-hour queues. I get really antsy and keep checking the time or shifting around. Sometimes I kind of want to jump in before it’s actually my turn.
